summary: H + H+ charge-exchange cross section in m^2 as a function of collision energy in eV. The default is a continuous composite of the Janev polynomial below 12.673175 keV and the Lindsay-Stebbings 2005 Table 1 fit above it, tabulated through 250 keV. freeman=True retains the independent Freeman-Jones analytic branch through 100 keV. Upper-range values clip with a RuntimeWarning; negative energies and non-scalar selectors are rejected.

capability: H + H+ charge-exchange cross section in m^2 from collision energy in eV using a published continuous composite or the Freeman-Jones comparison fit.
operation: Evaluate the H + H+ charge-exchange cross section
collision energies and branch selector -> cross section per energy
discovery.model: Continuous Janev/Lindsay-Stebbings 2005 composite by default; independent Freeman-Jones analytic branch under freeman=True; no runtime interpolation of tabulated data and no rate integration.
discovery.geometry: None; scalar material function of collision energy with no spatial axis (coordinate: collision energy in eV; output in m^2).
discovery.boundary: Energies finite and nonnegative. The default composite covers [0.1, 2.5e5] eV; Freeman-Jones covers [0.1, 1e5] eV. Values above the selected upper limit clip with RuntimeWarning; low values clip to 0.1 eV. freeman must be scalar.

identity.relation: H + H+ charge-exchange cross section: a continuous default composite with Janev below the 12.673175 keV crossing and Lindsay-Stebbings 2005 Table 1 above it, plus an independent Freeman-Jones analytic comparison branch.
identity.direction: collision energies and branch selector -> cross section per energy
identity.definition: Clip energy to [0.1, 2.5e5] eV for the default or [0.1, 1e5] eV for freeman=True. For the default, return exp(polyval(log(E), a))*1e-4 m^2 with the nine Janev coefficients for E <= 1.267317514018116e4 eV; above that value return (4.15-0.531*ln(E_keV))^2*(1-exp(-67.3/E_keV))^4.5*1e-20 m^2. For freeman=True return 1e-4*0.6937e-14*(1-0.155*log10(E))^2/(1+0.1112e-14*E^3.3) m^2. Above the selected upper limit emit RuntimeWarning and return the endpoint value.
identity.model: continuous two-source default composite with an independent Freeman-Jones comparison branch
identity.geometry: none; a scalar material function of collision energy
identity.coordinates: collision energy in eV; output cross section in m^2
identity.boundary: Finite nonnegative real energies; scalar freeman selector; default domain [0.1, 2.5e5] eV, Freeman-Jones domain [0.1, 1e5] eV; upper clipping emits RuntimeWarning and lower clipping is silent.
assumptions: The Janev coefficients and Freeman-Jones constants retain their declared arithmetic.

Lindsay and Stebbings (2005), Table 1 and section 4.1, define the high-energy fit and its stated reliability; this repository does not relabel that published fit as an independent experimental validation.
The two fits agree at 12.67317514018116 eV to numerical precision, so the default branches there without an interpolation gap.
The Lindsay-Stebbings Table 1 range is 0.005-250 keV; claims outside that range are not supported by this fit.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: Collision energies at which the cross section is evaluated.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative real values. Low values clip to 0.1 eV. The default high limit is 2.5e5 eV; the Freeman-Jones high limit is 1e5 eV. Values above the selected limit clip and emit RuntimeWarning.

inputs.name: freeman
inputs.description: Branch selector: Freeman-Jones when truthy; the continuous Janev/Lindsay-Stebbings composite otherwise.
inputs.constraints: Scalar interpreted as truth value; arrays are rejected. Default false selects the composite.

outputs.name: cross_section_m2
outputs.description: Charge-exchange cross section, one value per energy.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive on both clipped branches.

preconditions: The caller accepts that values below 0.1 eV use the lower endpoint and values above the selected upper limit use the upper endpoint with RuntimeWarning.
The caller uses freeman=True only when the Freeman-Jones comparison model is intended.
supported: The default H + H+ cross section from 0.1 eV through 250 keV, with the two published fits joined at 12.673175 keV.
The independent Freeman-Jones analytic branch through 100 keV.
Scalar and arbitrary-shape array evaluation with scalar branch selection.
excluded: No Maxwellian rate integral is performed here; the separate rate entry owns that operation.
Molecular hydrogen and other species are different relations.
No experimental validation beyond the cited published parameterization and its stated reliability is established.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError naming energy_ev for non-real, non-finite or negative energy inputs, or naming freeman when that selector is an array rather than a scalar. There is no other failure mode.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Valid inputs return finite positive values. Energy above the selected upper limit emits RuntimeWarning and returns the endpoint value.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the relation has no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no cross section.

example.description: Evaluate the default composite and Freeman-Jones comparison branch, verify source-range high-energy values, endpoint warnings and invalid inputs.
example.code:
import warnings
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_cross_section

energy = np.array([0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 1.0e4, 1.267317514018116e4, 3.0e4, 1.0e5])
composite = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_cross_section(energy)
assert composite.shape == energy.shape
assert np.all(np.isfinite(composite)) and np.all(composite > 0.0)
freeman = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_cross_section(energy, freeman=True)
assert np.all(np.isfinite(freeman)) and np.all(freeman > 0.0)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    clipped = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_cross_section(np.array([0.01, 0.1, 3.0e5, 2.5e5]))
assert len(caught) == 1 and issubclass(caught[0].category, RuntimeWarning)
assert clipped[0] == clipped[1] and clipped[-1] == clipped[-2]
try:
    evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_cross_section(np.array([1.0, -0.5]))
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'nonnegative' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('a negative energy must be rejected')
try:
    evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_cross_section(energy, freeman=np.ones((2, 2)))
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'freeman' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('an array branch selector must be rejected')
example.expected: Finite positive default and Freeman-Jones values; a continuous default join; one warning and exact endpoint repetition above 250 keV; ValueError for negative energy and an array selector.

scope: The default composite matches independent evaluations of the Janev and Lindsay-Stebbings formulas on both sides of the join and is continuous there.
At 30, 50, 80 and 100 keV the default is compared with Lindsay-Stebbings values using the paper-stated 11% reliability above 6 keV; the old clipped endpoint fails this check.
The Freeman-Jones branch matches its independent analytic expression and differs from the default composite.
Upper endpoint clipping and RuntimeWarning are covered for both the default and Freeman-Jones branches; the lower endpoint clips without a warning.
Input tests reject nonfinite, negative, boolean, complex and numeric-string energies and array-valued branch selectors.
The default callable remains a valid cross_section_m2 port for maxwellian-relative-speed-rate-average.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The tests establish formula evaluation, source-range agreement at the sampled high energies, the continuous join, clipping/warning semantics and input failures. Lindsay and Stebbings (2005) is read as the published parameterization and reliability statement; no independent experimental re-fit or rights decision is established.
known_limitations: The default uses the Janev fit below 5 eV, while the Lindsay-Stebbings Table 1 begins at 5 eV; the composite is not validated below 5 eV by the published table.
The Lindsay-Stebbings Table 1 ends at 250 keV; values above 250 keV warn and repeat the endpoint rather than extrapolate.

The paper states about 11% reliability above 6 keV, with a separate almost 30% theory-versus-measurement discrepancy at 100 keV. The fit difference and that discrepancy are not a newly derived uncertainty budget.
The Freeman-Jones branch is an independent comparison fit, not the default and not a correction to the composite.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
